$about: Declarative input for scripts/build-photos.mjs. See REDESIGN-PLAN.md section 7.
Sources live in assets/photos-source/ and are never published: Vite copies public/ verbatim,
and the 15 originals are 41MB. Only the derivatives named here reach dist/.
Crop boxes are in SOURCE pixels. Every source is 4000x2252, EXIF orientation 1.
Consent: participants signed off on appearing in IFN marketing material (founder ruling 2026-08-09).
Venue: Capital Factory was rebranded Station Austin. Its signage in these frames is dated, not dishonest.
Gallery round, 2026-08-10. Ten of the fifteen sources now ship. Two feed the landing page as before, one
new landing page slot carries the FounderStory image, and ten frames are grouped into the three evenings
the folder actually contains: 2026-02-26, 2026-04-23 and 2026-07-23. Those three dates are the only
evidence of recurrence this site owns that is not a sentence of copy, which is why the grouping is
declared here as data and emitted, rather than left for a gallery component to hardcode.

budget.$note: REDESIGN-PLAN.md section 7. Measured at build, never estimated.
$landingNote: Every avif tier a 1440px viewport at 1x actually selects on the landing route, named as data.
The runner used to hardcode this list in JavaScript while carrying a comment claiming it did not,
and the comment was right about the hazard: a hand written list goes stale by printing PASS, which
is the worst direction for a check to fail in. It went stale twice in one round, once when the
FounderStory slot arrived and once when its placement widened from 576 to 904 CSS px and moved the
selected tier from 640 to 960. Adding a photographic slot to the landing page now means adding a
row here, and forgetting is a MISSING entry rather than a silently short total.

landingAt1440.why: full bleed band, the widest tier a 1440 viewport takes
the 2fr middle stop is about 600 CSS px
904 CSS px at 1x lands on the 960 tier
GalleryPreview stacked frame, about 470 CSS px
GalleryPreview lead frame, about 690 CSS px
GalleryPreview stacked frame, about 470 CSS px

$galleryNote: The gallery is a separate route, so it carries a separate budget rather than eating the landing page's.
256KB is every avif tile in the grid at once, which is what a visitor pays on arrival. Enlarged views are
excluded because they are fetched on interaction and most visitors never open one.

$note: Baked in at build so the grade costs nothing at runtime.
whiteBalance is a per channel multiplier applied with the levels move, not a separate pass.
blackPoint and whitePoint are fractions of full range: out = wb * (white - black) * in + black * 255.

april-2026.note: Daylight through a full height glass wall. Measured on the hero crop: mean RGB 93.6 / 94.8 / 91.7, so red sits 1.3 percent over green and blue 3.4 percent over green. That is neutral inside any correction worth applying, so none is applied.

february-2026.note: REDESIGN-PLAN.md section 7 calls this night a green cast. The files do not agree and this is the measurement that corrects it: on the reserve hero crop mean RGB is 61.4 / 64.3 / 77.6, so blue runs 21 percent over green and red 4.5 percent under it. The cast is blue, not green. A full grey world correction would be [1.0475, 1.0, 0.8286] and it erases the night by neutralising a window that really is that colour, so this is half of it, which reads as a cool room rather than a lavender one. Verified by rendering the reserve hero, not by argument. No February frame ships on day one.

july-2026.note: Evening interior under white LED strips. Measured on the reserve middle stop crop: mean RGB 126.1 / 118.1 / 114.0, so red runs 6.8 percent over green. That warmth is the room and correcting it out makes skin tones grey, so it is left alone. Checked by rendering. No July frame ships on day one.

slots.name: hero-band
cropNote: Full source width, so the vertical offset is the only free parameter and 585 is its maximum.
Bottom anchored: it drops the ductwork ceiling and keeps every seated person and the foreground chairs.
Checked against the plan's one design preference on this frame: after the grade the former venue gear
reads mid grey in the upper left and the brightest objects in the band are the two IFN screens and the
glass wall, so the dated logo is not the highest contrast object. Verified by rendering, not reasoned.
slots.alt: A dozen founders seated in a circle in conversation, photographed from behind the back row, with an IFN meetup slide on two screens and downtown Austin through a full height glass wall.

slots.name: how-it-works-middle
cropNote: Full source height, so the horizontal offset is the only free parameter and it is free across 1184px.
Rendered at 600, 900 and 1184 and compared. 600 slices a foreground shoulder at the left edge and 1184
slices a head at it. 900 is the only candidate where no subject is cut by an edge the original did not
already cut: the listener at left, the speaker mid gesture and the listener at right are all whole.
slots.alt: One founder mid gesture in a small seated circle with the others listening, an IFN meetup slide on the screen behind them and the city through the window.

slots.name: founder-story
cropNote: REDESIGN-PLAN.md section 7 lists this frame as still excluded, and that status is REVERSED here rather
than ignored. The reason it was excluded is quoted exactly: 'Six people among a dozen empty chairs.
Honest and self-defeating at the same time.' That is a judgment about a MARKETING frame, and it is
correct about one. This slot is not a marketing frame. FounderStory is headed 'The meetups came first'
and its first sentence is that IFN began as a room full of international founders and that everything
else came afterwards. A room in February with a handful of people in it and the chairs still empty is
what that sentence looks like. The quality that disqualified the frame as a hero is the quality that
qualifies it as the editorial one, so the original reason is narrowed in scope rather than contradicted.
Section 7 needs amending to match; that is named in the handover rather than left for a reader to spot.
The crop is the full frame at exactly 16:9. Source is 4000x2252, so top=1 gives 4000x2250 and every tier
divides with no drift. Three candidates were rendered at 1152 and compared, not reasoned about:
3:2 at left=0    every person whole, but the former venue gear lands dead centre.
3:2 at left=311  gear moves to about 40 percent of the width, and the leftmost man is sliced by the edge.
16:9 full frame  gear sits at about 41 percent, nobody is cut, and it holds the most empty chairs.
The last one wins on all three counts at once. It also keeps the plan's stated design preference on the
former venue mark without paying a person for it: the two lit IFN screens are the brightest objects in
the frame and the gear is neither centred nor the highest contrast thing in it.
sizesNote: WIDENED 2026-08-10 from 576px to 904px, and the 1920 tier was added in the same edit because the
two numbers are one decision. A design pre-flight measured the 576px placement at 42 percent of the
section width with about 640px of empty ground beside it and called it decoration in a gap rather
than a change of rhythm. 904px is the full FounderStory grid at lg: the 36rem prose track, the
3.5rem gutter and the 17rem rail track, so the frame becomes the floor of the section rather than a
thumbnail parked under one column of it.
The old note here argued 576 was the widest placement with 2x device pixels behind it, which was true
against a ladder that stopped at 1280. That was a build artifact setting a composition decision, so
the ladder moved instead: 904 CSS px at 2x needs 1808, the source is 4000x2252 and the global hard
cap is 1920, so a 1920 tier is buildable with no new source and no cap violation. It gives 2.12x.
A 1440 viewport at 1x selects the 960 tier, which is what the landing page budget below is measured on.
slots.alt: Two small groups of people talking across a large open room with rows of empty chairs around them, under a steel and ductwork ceiling, with lit IFN meetup slides on two screens.

slots.name: gallery-feb-sign
cropNote: Not the full frame. Two heads are cut by the bottom edge of the source, and a head sliced by the frame
edge is the one thing a gallery tile cannot carry off at 640px. Height 1800 from top=0 drops them.
left=400 was picked against renders at 200, 400 and 600: 200 keeps a dead black doorway at the left,
600 pushes the second screen off the edge. 400 holds the lit sign, the second screen, the pendant lamp,
both reflections in the window glass and the night skyline.
slots.alt: An IFN meetup slide lit on a wall mounted screen at night under a pendant lamp, with a second screen to the left and the slide reflected twice in the window glass over the city.

slots.name: gallery-apr-circle
cropNote: Full frame at exactly 16:9. Every gallery frame is presented uncropped unless something in it has to go,
because a gallery's job is to show the photograph and a crop there is an argument the tile cannot make.
slots.alt: About a dozen people seated in a wide circle in conversation, with daylight coming through a full height glass wall behind them and an IFN meetup slide on a screen at the left.

slots.name: gallery-apr-room
cropNote: The hero band's source, shown here as the whole photograph rather than as the 2.4:1 band the hero crops
out of it. That is the point of the pairing and not a duplication: the page prints a band with the
ceiling removed, the gallery prints the picture that band was cut from. The extra derivatives are named
in the byte report so the cost of that choice is visible rather than absorbed.
slots.alt: A circle of people talking across a wide open floor, photographed from behind the back row, with an IFN meetup slide on two screens and downtown Austin through the windows.

slots.name: gallery-apr-listening
cropNote: Selected over 20260423_184523.jpg, which is the same framing four seconds earlier. Both were rendered at
the 640 tile width and compared there rather than at full size, because that is where the tile is read:
184523 gives roughly a quarter of the frame to empty foreground chairs, and 184527 fills that space with
people. The edge cuts that made 184523 look the safer of the two at full resolution are invisible at 640.
slots.alt: A seated circle of people listening, several of them in the foreground with their backs to the camera, with the room's windows and IFN screens behind.

slots.name: gallery-apr-gesture
cropNote: The HowItWorks middle stop's source, shown whole. Same relationship as gallery-apr-room: the page prints
a 1093:874 crop of one conversation, the gallery prints the frame it was taken from.
slots.alt: One person mid gesture speaking to a small seated circle, the others turned toward them, with an IFN meetup slide on the screen behind and the city through the glass.

slots.name: gallery-apr-floor
cropNote: Section 7 returned this frame to the pool and then passed over it for the hero band, on the grounds that
the laptop dominates the foreground. In a gallery that is what recommends it: it is the only frame shot
from the front of the room looking back, so it is the only one that shows the floor, the distance and
the person running the evening's vantage point. It adds a scale the other five April frames do not have.
slots.alt: The meetup seen from behind a laptop on a stand at the front of the room, the group seated in a circle in the distance across a wide polished concrete floor.

slots.name: gallery-apr-group
cropNote: REDESIGN-PLAN.md section 7 lists this frame as still excluded, and that status is REVERSED here rather
than ignored. The reason is quoted exactly: 'a posed line-up is a different kind of picture from the
documentary frames this page is built on, and mixing the two is how a page starts looking like a
brochure.' That is correct, and it is a statement about the LANDING PAGE. This frame does not go on the
landing page and no slot here puts it there. A dated gallery of an evening is the one surface where an
end of night group photograph is the native genre rather than an intruder in someone else's, and it is
the only frame in the folder that shows how many people actually came. The exclusion is narrowed to the
landing page rather than lifted. Section 7 needs amending to match; that is named in the handover.
The timestamp is 20:18, roughly ninety minutes after the other five April frames, so it also closes the
evening in the gallery's own reading order.
slots.alt: A line of people standing shoulder to shoulder facing the camera in front of an IFN meetup screen at the end of the evening.

slots.name: gallery-jul-standing
cropNote: Full frame. The only frame from the third evening with people in it, and the only frame in the whole
folder of people standing rather than seated, which is what the meetup looks like before it starts.
slots.alt: Three people standing and talking with drinks in hand in a bright open lobby, an IFN meetup slide on the screen behind them.

slots.name: gallery-jul-screen
cropNote: Section 7 excludes this source, and the exclusion is NARROWED here rather than lifted. Its reason is a
wall of national and service flags, which for a brand addressing people arriving from other countries is
a signal not to send by accident, and section 7 notes in the same row that 'the left crop of 190952 is
clean'. This is that crop, cut to the measurement rather than to the sentence: the flags begin at source
x=1971 and the illuminated eagle at roughly x=2657, so a crop ending at x=1970 excludes both, and the
rendered result was checked for a clipped wing before this box was written down. The flags reason stands
in full against the uncropped frame and against 20260723_175654.jpg, which stays excluded.
top=820 was chosen against renders at 300, 560 and 820. 300 fills a third of the frame with cable trays
and a ceiling diffuser, 560 clips the top of the screen housing, 820 holds the whole projection screen,
both planters, the blinds and the reflection in the floor.
This frame is here on its own merits and not to make a group of one look less thin: it is the only
quiet, uncluttered, brightly lit frame in the folder and the only one where the IFN slide is the subject
rather than a light source behind someone's head. Its timestamp is 19:09:52, thirteen seconds after
gallery-jul-standing, so it is a quiet corner DURING the evening and the alt text does not claim it is
the room before anyone arrived.
slots.alt: An IFN meetup slide projected on a pull down screen in a quiet corner of the room, two potted plants beside it and the ceiling lights reflected in the polished floor.

slots.name: hero-band-reserve
cropNote: Standing fallback for the hero band, same slot and same ratio, so a swap is one status edit.
Top anchored: it keeps the lit sign, the pendant lamp, the two reflections in the window glass and the
night skyline, and it drops the two partial heads along the bottom edge of the source.
slots.alt: The IFN meetup slide lit on a screen at night, reflected twice in a window over the faintly lit skyline.

slots.name: how-it-works-middle-reserve
cropNote: Swap ready alternate for the middle stop at the same ratio. Prepared, not selected.
Section 7 files this frame under reserve on redundancy grounds. It is worth a second look: it is the
only close range frame of people from a different evening than the hero band, it carries no third party
branding, and swapping it in would separate the two day one photographs by date as well as by subject,
which is the residual risk section 10 leaves open. That is a selection call for the founder, not for the
pipeline, so it ships as reserve and the crop box is here so the decision costs one word.
slots.alt: Three founders standing with drinks mid conversation, an IFN meetup slide on the screen behind them.

$note: The audit record for every source that has NO slot above. Not built, by design: a frame with no slot has
no ratio, so inventing a crop box for it would be inventing a layout. Give it a slot above and it builds.
Rewritten 2026-08-10 for the gallery round. The invariant this list exists to keep is that a source appears
EXACTLY ONCE across the slots above and this pool. A source that ships from a slot while a pool row still
calls it excluded makes the whole audit record unreadable, because nothing tells the next reader which of
the two is authoritative. Ten of the fifteen sources now have a slot and have left the pool. Five remain,
and every reason below is a reason that survives the gallery, not one left over from a rule that changed.
Three exclusions were REVERSED to build this round, all three narrowed in scope rather than contradicted,
and each carries its argument in the cropNote of the slot that now uses it, not here:
meetups/20260226_184622.jpg  -> founder-story        (was excluded as a marketing frame; this is not one)
meetups/20260423_201820.jpg  -> gallery-apr-group    (was excluded from the landing page; still is)
venue/20260723_190952.jpg    -> gallery-jul-screen   (flags reason stands; the crop ends before them)
REDESIGN-PLAN.md section 7 still records all three as excluded and needs amending to match what ships.

returned-to-pool.reason: Consent and venue rulings void the old exclusion. Still not selected, now against a gallery too: the former venue logo is the composition itself, and the February night already ships two frames that are about the room and the sign rather than about the wall.

Consent and venue rulings void the old exclusion. Still not selected: the former venue gear is the largest and highest contrast object in the frame and one person in profile is the only subject, so it is a photograph of a logo in an evening that already ships six photographs of people.

reserve.reason: The frame the accent hue was sampled from. Redundant with gallery-feb-sign, which is the same subject on the same night better lit and without the exit sign competing with the slide.

The same framing as gallery-apr-listening four seconds earlier. Both were rendered at the 640 tile width and compared there; this one gives about a quarter of the tile to empty foreground chairs. Held as the swap if 184527 is ever objected to.

excluded.reason: A wall of national and service flags across the centre of the frame, with the illuminated venue eagle behind them. For a brand addressing people arriving from other countries that is a signal not to send by accident. The reason is independent of the 2026-08-09 consent and venue rulings and of the 2026-08-10 gallery, and unlike 190952 there is no crop of this composition that excludes the flags: they run from roughly x=1750 to x=3050 of 4000 with the eagle between them, so cutting them out cuts out the subject. The founder can overrule this in one word; the pipeline will not do it silently.
